general_information.Description: Course is aimed at study of the fundamentals of financial markets and financial instruments, the features of the formation of modern financial markets, on the practical application of financial instruments, the types of financial institutions and their roles and functions in the financial markets Upon successful completion, students will have the knowledge and skills to: * demonstrate a working knowledge of financial terms and concepts analyse how financial markets and instruments operate and how they can be used to achieve economic objectives; * understand and criticaly engage in profits and risks faced by investors and strategies to control these profits and risks; * demonstrate the ability to think independently, reflectively and analytically for work in regulating the financial sector, financial institutions or various areas of government. Topics include: Debt, equity, derivative markets, commercial bank, non-bank operation.
general_information.StudentTasks: 1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 2. Actively participate in class activities 3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes 5. Read the textbook in advance 6. Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and materials of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.
general_information.Tools: - Textbook and all learning materials provided on FLM - Internet

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the basic functions and structures of the major financial markets and financial institutions
Understand the simple models for determining the pricing and behavior of interest rate, foreign exchange, securities, derivatives
Understand the key role of central bank plays in the financial systems and how does central bank conduct monetary policy
Understand the regulatory and risk management issues of financial institutions
Analyze and evaluate the current financial market news and issues and their implications
Demonstrate the ability to produce a clear oral report and/or academic written report and deliver presentations on topics related to financial markets and institutions
Practice ability to work as part of an effective team to prepare report and presentation

constructive_questions.Name: Group 1 - discussion chapter 1
constructive_questions.Details: Explain the meaning of surplus units and deficit units. Provide an example of each. Which types of financial institutions do you deal with? Explain whether you are acting as a surplus unit or a deficit unit in your relationship with each financial institution.

constructive_questions.Name: Group 2 - Discussion chapter 1
constructive_questions.Details: Distinguish between primary and secondary markets. Distinguish between money and capital markets.

constructive_questions.Name: Group 3 - discussion chapter 1
constructive_questions.Details: Commercial banks use some funds to purchase securities and other funds to make loans. Why are the securities more marketable than the loans in the secondary market?

constructive_questions.Name: Group 1 - discussion chapter 2
constructive_questions.Details: If the federal government planned to expand the space program, how might this change affect interest rates?

constructive_questions.Name: Group 2 - Discussion chapter 2
constructive_questions.Details: What is the difference between the nominal interest rate and the real interest rate? What is the logic behind the implied positive relationship between expected inflation and nominal interest rates?

constructive_questions.Name: Group 3 - discussion chapter 2
constructive_questions.Details: Would increasing the money supply growth place upward or downward pressure on interest rates? Explain in more detail.

constructive_questions.Name: Group 1 - Discussion chapter 3
constructive_questions.Details: - Do investors in high tax brackets or those in low tax brackets benefit more from tax-exempt securities? Why? - At a given point in time, which offers a higher before-tax yield: municipal bonds or corporate bonds? Why? - Which has the higher after-tax yield? If taxes did not exist, would Treasury bonds offer a higher or lower yield than municipal bonds with the same maturity? Why?

constructive_questions.Name: Group 2 - Discussion chapter 3
constructive_questions.Details: Explain how a yield curve would shift in response to a sudden expectation of rising interest rates, according to the pure expectations theory.

constructive_questions.Name: Group 3 - Discussion chapter 3
constructive_questions.Details: If a downward-sloping yield curve is mainly attributed to segmented markets theory, what does that suggest about the demand for and supply of funds in the short-term and long-term maturity markets?

constructive_questions.Name: Group 1 - Discussion & Exercises chapter 6
constructive_questions.Details: 1. Interpret the following statements made by Wall Street analysts and portfolio managers. “Money markets are not used to get rich, but to avoid being poor.” 2. Assume an investor purchased a 6-month T-bill with a USD10,000 par value for USD9,000 and sold it 90 days later for USD9,100. What is the yield? 3. A money market security with a par value of USD10,000 sells for USD8,816.60. Given that the security has a maturity of two years, what is the investor’s required rate of return?

constructive_questions.Name: Group 2- Discussion & Exercises chapter 6
constructive_questions.Details: 1. Interpret the following statements made by Wall Street analysts and portfolio managers. “Until conditions are more favorable, investors are staying on the sidelines.” 2. A money market security that has a par value of USD10,000 sells for USD8,816.60. Given that the security has a maturity of two years, what is the investor’s required rate of return? 3. You paid USD98,000 for a USD100,000 T-bill maturing in 120 days. If you hold it until maturity, what is the T-bill yield? What is the T-bill discount?

constructive_questions.Name: Group 3 - Discussion & Exercises chapter 6
constructive_questions.Details: 1. Interpret the following statements made by Wall Street analysts and portfolio managers. “My portfolio is overinvested in stocks because of the low money market rates.” 2. constructive_questions.Name: Group 1 - Exercises chapter 1-3
constructive_questions.Details: **1. Nominal Rate of Interest** Suppose the real interest rate is 6 percent and the expected inflation rate is 2 percent. What would you expect the nominal rate of interest to be? **2. Forward Rate** Assume that, as of today, the annualized interest rate on a three-year security is 10 percent and the annualized interest rate on a two-year security is 7 percent. Use this information to estimate the one-year forward rate two years from now. **3. After-Tax Yield** Determine how the after-tax yield from investing in a corporate bond is affected by higher tax rates, holding the before-tax yield constant. Explain the logic of this relationship.

constructive_questions.Name: Group 2 - Exercises chapter 1-3
constructive_questions.Details: **1. Real Interest Rate** Suppose that Treasury bills are currently paying 9 percent and the expected inflation rate is 3 percent. What is the real interest rate? **2. After-Tax Yield** You need to choose between investing in a one-year municipal bond with a 7 percent yield and a one-year corporate bond with an 11 percent yield. If your marginal federal income tax rate is 30 percent and no other differences exist between these two securities, which would you invest in? **3. Commercial Paper Yield** A corporation is planning to sell its 90-day commercial paper to investors by offering an 8.4 percent yield. If the three-month Treasury bill’s annualized rate is 7 percent, the credit risk premium is estimated to be 0.6 percent, and there is a 0.4 percent tax adjustment, then what is the liquidity premium on the commercial paper?

constructive_questions.Name: Group 3 - Exercises chapter 1-3
constructive_questions.Details: **1. Nominal Rate of Interest** Suppose the real interest rate is 6 percent and the expected inflation rate is 2 percent. What would you expect the nominal rate of interest to be? **2. Forward Rate** Assume that, as of today, the annualized two-year interest rate is 13 percent and the one-year interest rate is 12 percent. Use this information to estimate the one-year forward rate. **3. Deriving Current Interest Rates** Assume that interest rates for one-year securities are expected to be 2 percent today, 4 percent one year from now, and 6 percent two years from now. Using only pure expectations theory, what are the current interest rates on two-year and three-year securities?

constructive_questions.Name: Group 1 - Exercises chapter 6-7
constructive_questions.Details: **1. Effective Yield** A U.S. investor obtains British pounds when the pound is worth USD1.50 and invests in a one-year money market security that provides a yield of 5 percent (in pounds). At the end of one year, the investor converts the proceeds from the investment back to dollars at the prevailing spot rate of USD1.52 per pound. Calculate the effective yield. **2. Return on NCDs** Phil purchased an NCD a year ago in the secondary market for USD980,000. The NCD matures today at a price of USD1 million, and Phil received USD45,000 in interest. What is Phil’s return on the NCD? **3. Inflation-Indexed** Treasury Bond An inflation-indexed Treasury bond has a par value of USD1,000 and a coupon rate of 6 percent. An investor purchases this bond and holds it for one year. During the year, the consumer price index increases by 1 percent every six months. What are the total interest payments that the investor will receive during the year?

Given that the security has a maturity of two years, what is the investor’s required rate of return? **3. Inflation-Indexed** Treasury Bond Assume that the U.S. economy experienced deflation during the year and that the consumer price index decreased by 1 percent in the first six months of the year and by 2 percent during the second six months of the year. An investor purchases the stock on margin, paying USD30 per share and borrowing the remainder from the brokerage firm at 10 percent annualized interest. If, after one year, the stock is sold at a price of USD60 per share, what is the return to the investor?

constructive_questions.Name: Group 2 - Exercises chapter 10-12

An investor purchases the stock on margin, paying USD50 per share and borrowing the remainder from the brokerage firm at 12 percent annualized interest. If, after one year, the stock is sold at a price of USD90 per share, what is the return to the investor?

The stock pays an annual dividend of USD0.80 per share, and after one year you are able to sell it for USD65. Calculate your return on the stock.
